relevant_locations.role: Type checking and handling of response chunk

llm_context.input_body: No body provided in issue description.

generated_output.summary: When a developer passes a raw ArrayBuffer to res.send(), Express treats it as a generic object and serializes it to an empty JSON object '{}' instead of sending it as binary data.
generated_output.root_cause_analysis: In lib/response.js, the 'object' type check only checks ArrayBuffer.isView(chunk) to identify binary views (like Uint8Array). It lacks a check for raw 'ArrayBuffer' instances (e.g., chunk instanceof ArrayBuffer). Consequently, raw ArrayBuffers fall through to the JSON serialization logic, resulting in an empty JSON object response.

step_by_step_plan.title: Inspect res.send in lib/response.js
step_by_step_plan.description: Inspect the res.send method in lib/response.js and locate the switch (typeof chunk) block. Identify where ArrayBuffer.isView(chunk) is used to handle binary views.

step_by_step_plan.title: Add ArrayBuffer Instance Check
step_by_step_plan.description: Modify the condition in the object case of res.send to check if chunk is an instance of ArrayBuffer (using chunk instanceof ArrayBuffer). If it is, convert it to a Node.js Buffer using Buffer.from(chunk) and set the content type to binary using this.type('bin') before sending.

step_by_step_plan.title: Add Regression Tests in test/res.send.js
step_by_step_plan.description: Add a new test suite or test case in test/res.send.js that calls res.send(new ArrayBuffer(10)) and asserts that the response has the 'Content-Type' header set to 'application/octet-stream' and contains the correct binary payload.

step_by_step_plan.title: Run Tests and Verify
step_by_step_plan.description: Execute the test suite using the command npm test to verify that the new test passes and no regressions are introduced in other response-sending behaviors.

structured_concepts.short_explanation: An ArrayBuffer represents a generic, fixed-length raw binary data buffer. ArrayBuffer.isView() returns true only for views like TypedArrays (e.g., Uint8Array) or DataView, but false for the raw ArrayBuffer itself.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: Developers need to understand this distinction because APIs handling binary data must check for both the raw buffer container and its views to correctly process binary payloads.
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: The bug occurs because the code only checks ArrayBuffer.isView(chunk), completely missing raw ArrayBuffer instances and letting them fall through to JSON serialization.

structured_concepts.short_explanation: Node.js Buffers can be created directly from an ArrayBuffer using Buffer.from(arrayBuffer), which shares the same allocated memory without copying.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: This allows efficient conversion of standard web binary types (ArrayBuffer) into Node.js-native binary types (Buffer) for network transmission.
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: Once the ArrayBuffer is correctly identified, the existing fallback logic in res.send() will automatically convert it to a Buffer using Buffer.from(chunk) and calculate its correct byte length.

common_pitfalls: Do not use typeof chunk === 'ArrayBuffer' because typeof an ArrayBuffer is 'object'.
Avoid manually converting the ArrayBuffer to a string or manually copying bytes, as Buffer.from(chunk) handles this natively and efficiently.
Do not forget to ensure that the Content-Type is set to binary ('bin') when an ArrayBuffer is detected, matching the behavior of ArrayBuffer views.
